issue_context.title: The value returned by AsQueryable().FirstOrDefault is different between Net5.0 and Net6.0
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

I can confirm this is a regression from .NET 5. Root cause is a corner case in [EnumerableRewriter](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/122c438e0987bf7bfd2a4a02368353d3774ff963) that fails to map back to the correct IEnumerable method overload. The regression was triggered by #48886 which added new overloads for the First/Last/SingleOrDefault methods. We should try to fix this.

review_comments: Is calling `ApplyTypeArgs` too soon here? If there are multiple matching methods, isn't calling `MakeGenericMethod` on all the matches wasteful if we are just going to return one of them?

It's needed in that case as well, since we need to run the comparison on the specialized method parameters. 

One possibility I considered is have `ArgsMatch` returned the specialized method as an `out` parameter, but it seemed to needlessly complicate the code.
Is it possible to fix the issue in `ArgsMatch`? It seems odd that it would return `true` when the method takes a `TSource` as a parameter, and the `args` has an `Expression<Func<TSource, bool>>`.
I don't think the `ArgsMatch` method is doing anything incorrectly, this is an issue of picking the correct matching overload.
I assume we don't need to worry about perf here? This could be written without using Linq.
I suppose we could squeeze out a bit of extra performance, but I guess I simply mirrored convention in the particular class; we seem to be using Linq fairly liberally.
